topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and introduces its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution, depending on the cellular context and an individual's susceptibility.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the question of bad luck
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for environmental contributions to cancer rather than treating its occurrence as simply inevitable or random.

topics.label: Infection-driven carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to cancer, developing Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: DNA damage mechanisms of environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how their effects depend on biological processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutagenic initiation may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility, and a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the explanation of carcinogenesis with developmental susceptibility and then summarise the mechanisms already taught.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenicity can be obtained and why each approach has limits in establishing human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by consolidating its main lessons and relating them to everyday risk–benefit decisions.
